q: Who blocked Tennessee's 44-yard field goal on the final play of the 2009 game to save Alabama's 12–10 win?
x: Terrence Cody, nicknamed Mount Cody, got his left hand on Daniel Lincoln's kick. It was his second blocked field goal of the fourth quarter.

q: Alabama beat Tennessee 12–10 in 2009 without scoring a touchdown. How many field goals did Leigh Tiffin make?
x: Tiffin hit from 38, 50, 22 and 49 yards. That was every one of Alabama's 12 points.

q: In the 1979 Sugar Bowl's famous goal line stand, which Alabama linebacker stopped Mike Guman on fourth down?
x: Krauss met Guman in midair at the goal line. He was named the game's MVP, still the only linebacker to win it.

q: Which No. 1-ranked team did Alabama beat 14–7 in the 1979 Sugar Bowl?
x: No. 2 Alabama beat No. 1 Penn State and finished No. 1 in the AP poll, Bear Bryant's fifth national title.

q: Who was named MVP of the 1926 Rose Bowl, Alabama's first bowl game?
x: Brown caught two touchdown passes and made a key late tackle. George Wilson was Washington's star.

q: Alabama won the 1926 Rose Bowl 20–19. What was the score at halftime?
x: Alabama scored three touchdowns in less than seven minutes of the third quarter to take the lead.

q: Bear Bryant's 315th win in 1981 made him college football's winningest coach. Whose record did he pass?
x: Bryant passed Stagg with a 28–17 win in the Iron Bowl at Legion Field.

q: Bear Bryant switched Alabama to the wishbone in 1971. Which coach taught him the offense?
x: Bryant spent part of the summer of 1971 learning it from his friend Royal, whose Texas teams ran it.

q: Alabama unveiled its new wishbone offense in the 1971 opener, a 17–10 upset at which school?
x: USC had beaten Alabama 42–21 the year before. Bryant kept the switch secret until kickoff in Los Angeles.

q: In the 1993 Sugar Bowl, George Teague chased down a Miami player from behind and stripped the ball. Who was it?
x: The strip didn't count because Alabama was offside, but it kept Miami from scoring a touchdown.

q: Miami came into the 1993 Sugar Bowl riding how long a winning streak?
x: Alabama ended it 34–13 and won the national championship.

q: Who was named MVP of the 1993 Sugar Bowl, Alabama's 34–13 win over Miami?
x: Lassic scored two touchdowns as Alabama ran for 267 yards.

q: In the 2012 BCS title game, Alabama beat LSU 21–0. How many field goals did Jeremy Shelley make?
x: Shelley made kicks from 23, 34, 41, 35 and 44 yards, a bowl record, and scored 15 of Alabama's 21 points.

q: Who scored the only touchdown of the 2012 BCS National Championship Game?
x: Richardson broke a 34-yard touchdown run with 6:15 left. LSU finished with 92 total yards.

q: How many field goals did Alabama miss in its 9–6 overtime loss to LSU in the 2011 Game of the Century?
x: Alabama got its revenge two months later, 21–0 in the BCS title game.

q: In the 2018 national championship game, Alabama trailed Georgia 13–0 at halftime. Which quarterback did Nick Saban send in?
x: The true freshman replaced Jalen Hurts and threw three touchdown passes.

q: Who caught the 41-yard touchdown on 2nd and 26 to win the 2018 national title in overtime?
x: Smith was a freshman too. Three seasons later he won the Heisman Trophy.

q: Mark Ingram won Alabama's first Heisman in 2009 in the closest vote ever. By how many points did he beat Toby Gerhart?
x: The final count was 1,304 to 1,276.

q: Who was the first Alabama quarterback to win the Heisman Trophy?
x: Young won it in 2021, the year after DeVonta Smith, giving Alabama back-to-back winners.

q: Derrick Henry's 2015 season broke whose SEC single-season rushing record?
x: Henry had 1,986 rushing yards when he won the Heisman, and he wasn't done.

q: DeVonta Smith was the first wide receiver to win the Heisman since whom?
x: Howard won for Michigan in 1991. Smith won in 2020 after a 1,856-yard season.

q: In Nick Saban's first season, Alabama lost at home to which Sun Belt team?
x: Louisiana-Monroe won 21–14 on Nov. 17, 2007. Two years later Alabama won the national title.

q: Nick Saban was hired by Alabama in January 2007 away from which team?
x: He had already won a national title at LSU before going to the NFL.

q: Frank Thomas, who coached Alabama to titles in 1934 and 1941, played quarterback at Notre Dame for which coach?
x: Thomas also roomed with George Gipp. Wallace Wade picked him as his successor in 1931.

q: When Frank Thomas took over in 1931, he replaced Wallace Wade's single wing with which offense?
x: Thomas learned the shifting Notre Dame Box under Rockne. His first team went 9–1.

q: As a player, Bear Bryant was known as "the other end" opposite which future Hall of Famer?
x: Bryant played end on Frank Thomas's 1934 national championship team.

q: Bear Bryant's first game as Alabama's head coach, in 1958, was a 13–3 loss in Mobile to which team?
x: That first team still finished 5–4–1, more wins than the three seasons before it combined.

q: Bear Bryant's last game was a 21–15 win in the 1982 Liberty Bowl. Who was the opponent?
x: Bryant died about a month later, on Jan. 26, 1983.

q: Before coming home to Alabama in 1958, Bear Bryant coached which school?
x: He had coached Maryland and Kentucky too, but Texas A&M was his job when "Mama called."
